steps.what: Verify travel requirements, route facts and destination constraints
Choose tour sites and route sequence
Calculate travel intervals and check opening-time overlaps
Check and revise the final tour itinerary

tasks.design: Use the native itinerary builder in the tour operations system {OTHER} to calculate intervals for the guide's chosen stops. The guide verifies source conditions, chooses destinations and checks the complete itinerary; no supplier order or traveller dispatch is implied by a draft plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Chosen routes still require repeated timing arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: A component library can carry validated opening windows and travel durations.
tasks.still_hard: Weather, accessibility and group stamina can invalidate an arithmetically feasible route.
tasks.human_edge: The guide balances experience, safety and travellers' interests.
tasks.altitude: Route choices stay with the guide; repeated interval arithmetic shrinks.

evidence.claim: Lemax supports reusable tour components and itinerary building; the local time allocation is not its vendor testimonial.

assumptions: Boundary is planning one itinerary, before actual supplier reservations or customer dispatch. Those actions require separate timed and gated steps when included.

s1's guide verifies stop identifiers, addresses, opening dates and hours, transfer modes, journey durations, buffers and accessibility limits from current operator and destination information, including manual entry and missing-data research. No new catalogue capture is free.

Try the native builder first. s3 removes only explicit interval calculations, not route judgement. s4 retains full feasibility checking, manual correction of unsupported routes and ordinary saving. Excess repair lowers the estimate; existing runtime is not labour.
Shares are provisional model estimates rather than measured travel-operator facts.
unknowns: Coverage and freshness of the component library
Manual timing effort for the guide's route mix
research_questions: Can the native builder preserve overnight and seasonal opening constraints?
How much s3 effort is arithmetic rather than obtaining trustworthy durations?

already_counted.description: Verify and capture all timing inputs, inspect the full route and repair unsupported segments.

incremental.description: Maintain route component fields and test seasonal calendar changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 20 arithmetic points less 1.5 upkeep. Conservative new destination has uncertain transfers and sparse library coverage: retain 17 points of manual timing and remove only three points of supported opening-window arithmetic, giving 1.5 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sell a travel package with checked terms and a controlled booking

steps.what: Discuss the traveller's needs and package questions
Check catalogue availability and package conditions
Select the package and calculate its quoted price
Prepare the package's existing pre-contract information form
Check final package terms and present the information form
Decide whether to accept the final package offer
Commit the accepted travel package booking
Send the checked booking confirmation to the traveller

tasks.design: Configure catalogue filters, price calculations and the existing information-form template in the tour booking system {OTHER}. The guide checks the exact final offer and recipient before the traveller accepts it, then retains the actual booking transaction and confirmation send as separate actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing package fields are repeatedly found, totalled and copied into information forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native package records can populate fixed fields and calculate approved rates.
tasks.still_hard: Suitability, availability changes and unusual package conditions need personal checking.
tasks.human_edge: The guide explains trade-offs and establishes informed traveller agreement.
tasks.altitude: Sales advice and booking authority stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Lemax supports tour products and booking workflows; these task shares are model estimates, not measured customer savings.
The digest identifies pre-contract package information obligations; exact applicable national implementation needs local checking.

assumptions: Boundary is an in-person package sale already using a booking system and an existing pre-contract information form. Payment collection and separate supplier orders are not hidden in the booking click; add their own priced and gated actions if part of this guide's task.

s1 captures traveller needs. Existing catalogue owners supply product identifier, departure, services, price components, capacity, conditions and organiser details. s2 checks freshness and manually resolves missing values; s3 retains selection, special terms and manual price exceptions. No new supplier data maintenance is free.

Native filters remove three points of navigation from s2; calculation removes two points of existing price arithmetic from s3. s4 removes fixed-field transcription only. s5 retains complete meaning, price, recipient and cancellation-term checks plus manual form repair, and records the final offer version. No model composes legal terms.

s5 also approves the exact prospective booking payload and confirmation text/recipient. Any offer, price, recipient or acceptance change voids both action approvals and returns to s5 and s6. s7 is a real customer booking commitment, not an ordinary author save. Both its one point and the real one-point send remain fully retained; no save or send saving is claimed.
Focal baseline is 95 points; the traveller's five decision points do not enter guide savings. All shares are provisional. Ordinary draft saves are retained within preparation.
unknowns: Existing form preparation effort and native field coverage
Whether a separate payment or supplier commitment belongs to this guide
research_questions: Does each form field come from a verified package record?
Can a changed price invalidate the booking and recipient approvals?

already_counted.description: Check catalogue exceptions, package choice, final information and manual form repairs.

incremental.description: Maintain information-form mappings and test changed package conditions.

approvals.approved_version: s5 final offered package version, exact booking payload and traveller; acceptance must match, any change voids approval
s5 final offered package version, exact confirmation text and traveller address; resulting booking must match, any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 3 navigation, 2 arithmetic and 15 form-entry points: 20/95*100 minus 1.5 = 19.55. Conservative customised package retains nearly all checking and bespoke form work; only 0.5 navigation, 0.5 arithmetic and three fixed-form points disappear: 4/95*100 minus 1.5 = 2.71.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate received tour services and report findings to organisers

steps.what: Collect and verify evidence about services received on tour
Evaluate service shortcomings and decide findings
Write the service evaluation report

loop.purpose: Phrase already-decided findings for the organiser
loop.input: Guide-decided findings and verified evidence references
loop.output: Draft report retaining attribution and uncertainty
loop.check: Guide compares every finding to evidence and checks omissions, speaker attribution and unsupported blame
loop.stop: Missing evidence or two unsuccessful revisions returns to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Use the native report structure first; variable service narratives need wording beyond fixed fields

steps.what: Check and approve the final report and organiser recipient
Send the approved service report to the tour organiser

tasks.design: Keep the service evaluation with the guide and use a bounded drafting loop in {DOCS} only for wording the findings already decided. After the complete report and exact organiser address are checked, a native {EMAIL} action sends that approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each tour's service narrative is different even when the report headings repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can preserve the guide's findings while a fixed workflow handles an approved send.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting accounts and the severity of service failures require fair judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The guide distinguishes poor service from circumstances beyond the supplier's control.
tasks.altitude: The guide remains the evaluator and accountable report author.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a source-bound loop can assist wording of an existing service report; its assessment and alleged time gains require local validation.

assumptions: The task explicitly includes an actual report to a tour organiser. s1 includes collection, capture and verification of observations and feedback; no new traveller survey or automatic recording is assumed.

s2 supplies finding text, affected service, date, evidence reference, attribution, uncertainty and recommended follow-up. Missing fields are resolved manually in retained s1-s3 time. Native report templates come first; the loop handles only residual narrative.

s3 retains 16 points for drafting, source checking and repairs; s4 retains nine for complete report and recipient approval. Extra repair lowers the estimate. Ordinary author saves are included and ungated.

s5's one point is today's actual email composition/attachment/dispatch interaction, not a save to the author's document store. Exact text, attachment and recipient are bound after s4; edits invalidate approval. Delivery failure checking remains in s4's retained allowance, with excess failures reducing benefit.
The organiser reads the report in separate work; no downstream investigation saving or transferred review is claimed. Shares are model estimates.
unknowns: Whether disputed complaints need substantial manual rewriting
research_questions: Does the draft preserve uncertain and conflicting evidence?
Is actual dispatch effort large enough to justify a native send action?

already_counted.description: Evidence capture, full draft/source checks, repair and final recipient verification.

incremental.description: Maintain report instructions and test send approval binding.

approvals.approved_version: s4 exact final service report, attachment and organiser address; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes four wording points and one actual-send point, less 0.8 upkeep. Conservative disputed supplier accounts leave only 0.8 point of neutral wording reusable and 0.2 point of dispatch interaction removable after manual attachment handling: 1 minus 0.8 = 0.2.

tasks.short: Give grounded sightseeing and shopping advice

steps.what: Look up sightseeing and shopping options and current conditions
Select suitable sightseeing or shopping advice
Explain recommendations and answer traveller questions

tasks.design: Configure the destination catalogue in the tour operations system {OTHER} to filter by the guide's location, category and accessibility criteria. It surfaces existing records; the guide checks current conditions and personally explains the recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding relevant catalogue entries takes repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native search filters can shorten retrieval without generating destination facts.
tasks.still_hard: Preferences, local changes and unsuitable shopping incentives need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The guide adapts recommendations to the traveller and checks that the advice is understood.
tasks.altitude: Advice remains personal; catalogue navigation is shorter.

evidence.claim: TUI piloted catalogue-linked excursion shortlisting; it does not establish this guide's time saving or shopping advice quality.

assumptions: Boundary is a spoken request for sightseeing or shopping advice using an existing destination catalogue. It does not include selling, booking or sending a written itinerary. No advice log is invented.

Catalogue owners already maintain place identifier, address, category, opening information, access restrictions and update date. s1 checks these fields and manually verifies missing or stale facts; health-related preferences are discussed only as necessary without new recording.

Native filters first: five points removed are search navigation, leaving 15 for reading, checking freshness and fallback lookup. No gain is claimed for destination judgement or conversation. If no existing catalogue covers the place, manual lookup remains and the estimate must fall.
Shares and upkeep are provisional estimates, not observed customer measurements.
unknowns: Catalogue coverage for shopping and accessibility
Share of navigation versus source verification
research_questions: Can a saved filter find relevant entries without hiding restrictions?
How frequently does a live local change override the catalogue?

already_counted.description: Read source entries, verify current conditions and fall back to manual lookup.

incremental.description: Maintain saved filter categories and check catalogue freshness indicators.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes five navigation points less 0.7 upkeep. Conservative unfamiliar shopping district has sparse catalogue entries, so only 0.9 navigation point disappears and the guide retains almost all source searching: 0.9 minus 0.7 = 0.2.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
